statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-73500 (GO-2026-6107, GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3): TLS listeners created by NewTLSListener in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport did not enforce a handshake deadline, so an unauthenticated client that connected without sending a ClientHello held a goroutine and a tracking entry indefinitely, and many such connections could exhaust memory. It is fixed in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 3.5.33, 3.6.14 and 3.7.1 by a change to (*tlsListener).acceptLoop that sets a deadline around the handshake: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6107, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/22130, and for the 3.6 release line https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/22142. The Go vulnerability database lists NewListener, NewListenerWithOpts, NewTLSListener, NewTimeoutListener and tlsListener.acceptLoop in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport as the affected functions. We read every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, each matching its repository index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. In every version the four external-dns packages (external-dns, external-dns-dev, external-dns-fips and external-dns-fips-dev) and both architectures embed the same Go and module versions. Its Go build information lists the go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 module (v3.6.6 and v3.6.10 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13, v3.7.1 and v3.7.2 from 0.22.0-r0 on), but none of the builds links its transport package. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader, which finds runtime.main in every build, finds no function of go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport in any build, and a byte search of every program, which also catches inlined names, finds no symbol name of that package. As a positive control, we built test programs for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 v3.6.13, the last affected 3.6 release, that call NewTLSListener and NewListener. In them the same reader finds NewTLSListener, NewListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop, the function the fix changes, and the byte search finds symbol names of the transport package. None of the advisory's affected functions is present in any published build.

CVE-2026-73500 (GO-2026-6107, GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3): TLS listeners created by NewTLSListener in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport did not enforce a handshake deadline, so an unauthenticated client that connected without sending a ClientHello held a goroutine and a tracking entry indefinitely, and many such connections could exhaust memory. The flaw is in the go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport package and is fixed in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 3.5.33, 3.6.14 and 3.7.1 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6107, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/22130). We read the Go build information and the Go function table (.gopclntab) of /usr/bin/metrics-server, the one file the package ships, in every published metrics-server-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (29 versions, 0.8.1-r0 to 0.9.1-r2, x86_64 and aarch64; each download matched the index checksum). In each version the metrics-server, metrics-server-dev, metrics-server-fips and metrics-server-fips-dev packages are built with the same Go toolchain and the same module versions; the -fips packages are built in Go's FIPS 140-3 mode, and the -dev packages are linked without -w, so they keep the DWARF debug information that the metrics-server and metrics-server-fips programs drop (all four keep the Go symbol table). Every build lists the go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 module (v3.5.21 in 0.8.1-r0 to 0.8.1-r12, v3.6.11 in 0.9.0-r0 to 0.9.0-r3, v3.6.14 from 0.9.0-r4), but the only packages of that module with functions in the program are fileutil and logutil. No go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport function is in the function table of any build, including the advisory's vulnerable functions NewListener, NewListenerWithOpts, NewTLSListener, NewTimeoutListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop, while runtime.main is in every build. As a positive control, the same function-table search run on a small test program built with golang.org/x/crypto v0.54.0, golang.org/x/text v0.40.0 and go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 v3.6.13 finds go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport.NewTLSListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop. The vulnerable listener code is not compiled into metrics-server, so it is not present in any published build.

CVE-2026-73500 (GO-2026-6107, GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3): TLS listeners created by NewTLSListener in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3/transport set no handshake deadline, so an unauthenticated client that connects and never sends a ClientHello holds a goroutine and a tracking entry forever, and many such connections exhaust memory. It is fixed in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 v3.5.33, v3.6.14 and v3.7.1 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6107, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/22130, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/tag/v3.6.14, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/tag/v3.7.1). Read every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 44 builds, 1.18.1-0 to the current 1.22.0-16, for amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only), 87 packages, each checked against the index SHA256; no debug-symbol package is published for this source. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/alloy. Both architectures of a build carry the same Go and module versions, and no build replaces the module. The module is listed in every build (v3.6.7 in 1.18.1-0 and 1.18.1-1, v3.6.14 in 1.18.1-2 to 1.19.2-7, v3.7.1 from 1.20.1-0), but alloy does not use its listener code. Searched the function symbols of /usr/bin/alloy (go tool nm) in all 87 packages for the functions the advisory names as affected, transport.NewListener, NewListenerWithOpts, NewTLSListener, NewTimeoutListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop, including -fm method-value wrappers: none is present in any build, and no other listener function of the transport package is either. The only functions of the transport package that are linked are TLSInfo.ClientConfig and TLSInfo.baseConfig with their closures, which build a client TLS configuration. As a positive control, the same search on a small linux/amd64 program built with go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 v3.6.14 that calls transport.NewTLSListener finds NewTLSListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop, and runtime.main is present in every alloy build. The vulnerable code is not present.

It is fixed in go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 v3.5.33, v3.6.14 and v3.7.1 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6107, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/GHSA-6vch-q96h-7gc3, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/22130, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/tag/v3.6.14, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/tag/v3.7.1). Read every published alloy package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 44 builds, 1.18.1-0 to the current 1.22.0-16, for amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only), 87 packages, each checked against the index SHA256; no debug-symbol package is published for this source. Each package installs /usr/bin/alloy, its only ELF program, plus the default configuration /etc/alloy/config.alloy and an SPDX SBOM JSON file under /opt/docker/sbom. Both architectures of a build carry the same Go and module versions, and no build replaces the module. The module is listed in every build (v3.6.7 in 1.18.1-0 and 1.18.1-1, v3.6.14 in 1.18.1-2 to 1.19.2-7, v3.7.1 from 1.20.1-0), but alloy does not use its listener code. Searched the function symbols of /usr/bin/alloy (go tool nm) in all 87 packages for the functions the advisory names as affected, transport.NewListener, NewListenerWithOpts, NewTLSListener, NewTimeoutListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop, including -fm method-value wrappers: none is present in any build, and no other listener function of the transport package is either. The only functions of the transport package that are linked are TLSInfo.ClientConfig and TLSInfo.baseConfig with their closures, which build a client TLS configuration. As a positive control, the same search on a small linux/amd64 program built with go.etcd.io/etcd/client/pkg/v3 v3.6.14 that calls transport.NewTLSListener finds NewTLSListener and (*tlsListener).acceptLoop, and runtime.main is present in every alloy build. The vulnerable code is not present.
